# University of the Andes (Colombia)
The University of the Andes was founded in 1948 by Mario Laserna Pinzón amidst a period of political change and economic modernization in Colombia. It was established as the country's first nonsectarian and politically neutral university, modeled after the American university system, to provide Colombia with technically skilled professionals and liberal education essential for national development. The university began classes in 1949 with 80 students and emphasized a blend of technical knowledge and liberal arts, including a unique "three/two program" allowing students to complete part of their studies abroad at prestigious American universities through scholarships funded by industry and philanthropy. Despite political violence during the 1950s, the university maintained its neutrality and expanded academic offerings and recruitment of international faculty.
Administratively, the university operates as a nonprofit corporation with full university status granted in 1964. Its governance includes a Board of Trustees, a Board of Directors, a Rector, and Academic Councils overseeing its 14 academic units, which comprise 10 faculties and several interdisciplinary centers. The campus, located in Bogotá's historical center, combines restored industrial and religious buildings with modern facilities including extensive libraries and laboratories. The mascot, a goat named Seneca, symbolizes student life and traditions. The university maintains robust international exchange programs with over 119 partner institutions in 34 countries, supporting interdisciplinary study and research. Notable alumni include Colombian presidents, ministers, academics, and renowned professionals in arts and sciences.
